fields.current: Requires government ID to vote in person and the last four digits of an ID number on mail ballots. The state must offer a free voter ID card, make best efforts to verify voters' citizenship, and report results yearly.

evidence.excerpt: the voter shall present government-issued identification
if voting by mail, the voter shall provide the last four digits of a unique identifying number
Upon request by an eligible voter, the State shall provide, at no charge, a voter ID card for use in casting a ballot.
shall use best efforts to verify citizenship attestations using government data
shall annually report what percentage of each county's voter rolls have been citizenship-verified.

fields.explanation: Each element confirmed by legal text and LAO page 2.
fields.limitations: Could add that the official summary says mail ballots without matching digits would not count. See risk.

fields.current: The State Auditor audits the state and every county in odd-numbered years, counties report citizenship-verified shares yearly, and citizens may sue. No penalties or numeric targets.

evidence.excerpt: During every oddnumbered year, the California State Auditor shall audit
Citizens may seek judicial review and remedy of the State's or any county's compliance with this section.
report every year the percentage of registered voters in each county whose citizenship status has been verified.

fields.explanation: Audit, reporting and lawsuit right confirmed. No penalties appeared in the fetched text.
fields.limitations: 'No penalties or numeric targets' rests on absence in the reader's view of the text.

fields.current: Supporters' official argument says bipartisan voter ID builds trust, keeps mail voting, offers a free ID and adds citizenship checks.

evidence.excerpt: Voter ID is a common-sense reform to increase trust and participation in our elections.
Prop. 39 keeps mail ballots, extended polling hours and all other conveniences in place for voting accessibility.
this measure even guarantees every voter a FREE Voter ID if they want one.
Election officials will also be required to check voter rolls to ensure only citizens are registered.

fields.explanation: All points appear. 'Bipartisan' reflects signers who chair Democratic, Republican and Independent coalitions.

fields.current: Opponents' official argument says it adds costly barriers and could reject ballots from seniors, students and people who changed names.

fields.current: The measure does not say what happens when mail-ballot ID digits are missing or mismatched, which opponents say could lead to rejected ballots.

evidence.excerpt: Invalidates mail ballots if envelope does not include last four digits of a government-issued identification number
(e.g., if voter designates Social Security number for registration, but provides driver's license number on envelope,
Election officials shall only count a regular or provisional ballot after verifying the identity of the person voting
Elections officials would verify that the identification numbers provided on the ballot envelope match

fields.explanation: The Attorney General's official summary says such ballots would not count, and the text allows counting only after identity is verified. What the text lacks is any notice or cure process. LAO does not state the consequence.
fields.proposedText: The official summary says mail ballots without matching ID digits would not count, and the measure sets no notice or fix-it process. Opponents say valid ballots could be thrown out.

fields.current: LAO projects net costs, and studies find very little voter fraud to prevent. A possible gain in voter trust is unmeasured.

evidence.excerpt: Proposition 39 would increase state and local government costs each year by tens of millions of dollars
Finally, strict ID requirements have no effect on fraud – actual or perceived.

fields.explanation: LAO confirms costs. The NBER paper finds no effect of strict ID laws on fraud, actual or perceived. That is not the same as 'very little voter fraud to prevent', and it also bears on the trust claim.
fields.proposedText: LAO projects net costs, and a national study found strict ID laws had no effect on fraud, actual or perceived. A possible gain in voter trust is unmeasured.
